mean: the four-part structure of a story or essay
lit: open, develop, turn, conclude: the four steps of a well-built piece

story.text: The term comes from the craft of classical Chinese poetry. In a four-line quatrain (jueju), each line had its job: the first opens the scene, the second develops it, the third turns to something unexpected, and the last ties everything together. In Japan the same four steps were later applied to essays, speeches and, famously, four-panel comic strips.
story.source: Classical Chinese poetics: the structure of the jueju quatrain (起承転合 in Chinese)

use.how: A noun for the structure of a story, essay, speech or comic: 起承転結がある / はっきりしている / を意識して書く. Not for the steps of a task or process.
